text: Organic farming has both advantages and limitations compared to conventional agriculture. Studies published in Nature Plants show that organic yields are typically 20-25% lower per acre, which means more land is needed to produce the same amount of food. On the other hand, organic practices tend to build healthier soil over time, support greater biodiversity, and reduce synthetic pesticide exposure for farmworkers. The tradeoff between productivity and environmental sustainability is real, and the best approach likely involves integrating techniques from both systems rather than treating them as mutually exclusive philosophies.
